epoch_topic: the long exposure: what a single image keeps when it is held open far longer than anything in front of it lasts. Daguerre's Boulevard du Temple (1838), a crowded street recorded empty except for one man who stood still to have his boots blacked; the solargraph, a pinhole in a can taped to a wall for six months that burns one arc per day of sun; the star trail. Everything that moves is erased. Whatever holds still, or comes back every day, becomes the picture.
